assertion: In 2015, Alabama was ranked 45th among states on the fourth grade National Assessment of Educational Progress, but in the years that followed rose to 18th in 2019 and 13th in 2024.
inaccuracy: The 45th/18th ranks come from the Fordham report's passage about Mississippi. Warehouse NAEP grade 4 reading ranks for Alabama are 40th (2015), 48th (2019) and 33rd (2024) of 51.
sql: select year, jurisdiction_name, avg_score, rk from (select year, jurisdiction_name, avg_score, rank() over (partition by year order by avg_score desc) rk from edu.naep_scores where subject='RED' and grade=4 and variable_type='TOTAL' and jurisdiction<>0 and is_displayable=1) t where jurisdiction_name in ('Alabama','Mississippi')
independent_value: Fordham: 'Mississippi... rising from 45th... in 2015 to 18th in 2019. In 2024, it leapt another five spots'; Alabama ranked last in 2019. Governor's office (via Vaites) says reading rank moved 49th to 34th during Ivey's term.

assertion: After falling below the national average for fourth-grade reading between 2013 and 2022, the state is closing the gap again. Its 2024 average scale score was ... just two points below the national average.
inaccuracy: Warehouse shows 213.2 vs national public 214.3 (about 1 point); Fordham says 213, two points below.
sql: select year, jurisdiction_name, avg_score from edu.naep_scores where subject='RED' and grade=4 and variable_type='TOTAL' and jurisdiction in (0,1)

assertion: She raised $1.5 million ... She went back and got the state legislature to fund $6 million. ARI funding went from $58 million in 2013 to $40.7 million by 2018; this year ARI is funded at $152 million; every school gets $85,000 for a literacy coach.
independent_value: All figures appear in the Fordham report ($1.5M in 1998; $6M for 1999-2000; $58M to $40.7M; $152M for 2026-27; $85,000 per school)

assertion: Nearly 1,000 people are employed by the state to just focus on literacy.
speaker: Liana Loewus (Thomas B. Fordham Institute)
reason: Interviewee's figure; the Fordham report was searched and not found to state it.
why_not: The only '1,000' match in the Fordham report is a $1,000 teacher stipend, unrelated to staffing.
